While fishing hours are not considered, fishing earnings are considered for both the fishing earnings threshold and the fishing benefit rate. What are the fishing earnings threshold and fishing hours threshold? The fishing earnings threshold is the minimum amount of earnings you must have from fishing to be eligible for EI fishing benefits. It is the greater of:

$2,500

3.9% of the maximum insurable earnings (MIE) for the year ($54,200 for 2022)

For 2022, the fishing earnings threshold is $2,111.58. The fishing hours threshold is the minimum amount of time you must have spent fishing. It is the greater of:

$2,500

3.9% of the MIE for the year ($54,200 for 2022)

For 2022, the fishing hours threshold is 630 hours. You do not need to have met the fishing hours threshold to qualify for EI fishing benefits. The fishing earnings threshold is the only requirement to qualify for EI fishing benefits. Do I need to have worked in fishing in the same year I apply for fishing benefits? Yes, you must have worked in fishing in the same year you apply for fishing benefits. You cannot count fishing earnings from a previous year to meet the fishing earnings threshold. How do I calculate my fishing earnings? You can calculate your fishing earnings by adding the amount of income you earned from fishing. The amount of income you earned from fishing is usually shown in box 14 of your T4A slip. If you do not have a T4A slip, you can calculate your fishing earnings by subtracting your expenses from your revenue. What are my fishing expenses? Your fishing expenses are the costs you incur to earn income from fishing. They can include things like fuel, bait, and equipment. You can deduct these expenses from your revenue to calculate your fishing earnings. What are my fishing revenue? Your fishing revenue is the income you earn from fishing. It can include things like the sale of fish, the sale of fishing equipment, and any other income you earn from fishing. You can use this amount to calculate your fishing earnings. I worked in fishing in 2021 and 2022. Can I use my fishing earnings from both years to meet the fishing earnings threshold? No, you must have worked in fishing in the same year you apply for fishing benefits. You cannot count fishing earnings from a previous year to meet the fishing earnings threshold.
